name: Pacitrel
description: Pacitrel is the most prescribed pharmaceutical in GLMZ by volume — a second-generation anxiolytic that modulates the HPA axis and BCI-integrated stress response systems simultaneously, addressing both organic anxiety and the amplified stress load that comes from constant neural connectivity. Unlike older benzodiazepine derivatives, it does not cause sedation at standard doses and is considered safe for operation of most machinery and neural interfaces.
effects: Reduced cortisol and synthetic stress-hormone spikes
Decreased physical anxiety symptoms (tremor, elevated heart rate, hyperventilation)
side_effects: Mild emotional flattening at higher doses
Rebound anxiety on cessation after prolonged use
Reduced threat-assessment sensitivity — users may underreact to genuine danger
Sexual dysfunction in approximately 30% of long-term users
Interaction with BCI systems can cause input lag in high-stimulation environments
Psychological dependency extremely common — most users cannot imagine functioning without it
street_price: Φ18 per tablet (Φ90 monthly supply with corporate wellness plan)
cultural_context: Pacitrel is so ubiquitous that not being on it is considered mildly eccentric in Tier 3 and 4 circles. Corporate wellness programs subsidize it. Shelf clinics distribute generics. It is the chemical infrastructure of a society that demands its citizens function calmly under objectively anxiety-inducing conditions — surveillance, precarity, BCI overstimulation, ecological anxiety, chronic noise. Critics call it 'the consent pill' — a drug that makes the unacceptable feel manageable.
story_hooks: A Novafold logistics error results in a batch of Pacitrel being shipped without its active compound — suddenly, thousands of Tier 3 workers are experiencing raw, unmedicated anxiety for the first time in years, and the results are not what management expected
A Shelf organizer deliberately goes off Pacitrel to feel the full weight of their community's conditions, and uses the experience as fuel for a radicalization campaign — the corpos notice

A Tier 4 executive discovers their entire department has been on Pacitrel for so long that none of them have had an authentic stress response in years — and wonders if their risk assessments are dangerously compromised
